The idea is a one-day reversal: a coin that fell yesterday should bounce, so the factor should rise when yesterday's return is negative. The plainest reading is just the negative of yesterday's return, which I'll test first to see how much of it survives after the known reversal styles are removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain one-day reversal comes out with exactly zero incremental IC — as expected, the 1-day reversal style is fully absorbed, so "yesterday's fall" alone tells us nothing new. The bounce may be a slower, more persistent effect: a coin that has been falling over the last few days is more likely to give back than one that just dipped. I'll test the cumulative sum of daily returns over the last 5 days, negated, to see whether that adds anything.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0400
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0003 (t = 1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0004

The 5-day cumulative version has essentially nothing left after the styles too (+0.0003, t = 1.7), so the pattern-based reading of "has been falling" is not new information either. I'll try a different shape: the size of yesterday's drop relative to the coin's own recent daily volatility, so the bounce is measured as how unusual yesterday's fall was rather than its raw size — that strips out the volatility style.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0191
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0001 (t = -0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0008, 2023 +0.0001, 2024 -0.0008

Volatility-scaling flipped the sign to −0.0001 (t = −0.2), so on this history unusual-drop size is a bearish, not a bullish, signal — that is a real reversal effect, not the bounce the idea claims. I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the same shape.

What I found: the idea does hold in raw terms — coins that fell yesterday do bounce, with a rank IC of +0.0175 — but almost all of that is the known 1-day reversal style, so the incremental part is exactly zero. Measuring the bounce as a slow, cumulative drop over the last few days, or as the size of yesterday's fall relative to the coin's own recent volatility, both leave nothing after the known styles; the volatility-scaled version even points the wrong way. So the bounce is not an independent signal here, and I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping the sign to chase the data.

The idea is about dollar volume relative to its own recent history: when a coin's daily dollar volume is at a recent high, it should fall back. So I'll measure the current dollar-volume level against its own 20-day average, put the negative sign on the outside (since the idea says the high is bearish), and use USDT-denominated volume so it's comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0250
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0170 (t = 5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0220, 2023 +0.0199, 2024 +0.0116

The 5-day-over-20-day ratio already works: incremental IC +0.0170 with the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is weaker. The 5-day numerator may be too noisy, so I'll test the same idea with a longer 10-day baseline and a 5-day window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0192
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0084 (t = 3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0161, 2023 +0.0086, 2024 +0.0042

The 10-day baseline is clearly worse (+0.0084 versus +0.0170), so the 5-day numerator is the better choice. Now I'll check whether the window on the baseline matters: 20 days versus 60 days, same 5-day numerator.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

The 60-day baseline is worse again (+0.0096), so the 20-day baseline is the best of the three and I'm not going to spend another test on the same idea in a different form.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history. Measuring a coin's current dollar volume against its own 20-day average and negating it gives incremental IC +0.0170 (t = 5.9) with the same sign in all three periods, so it isn't a single-period artifact. Shorter windows (5-day over 10-day, 5-day over 60-day) both did worse, which suggests the signal is genuinely about how far the coin's dollar volume is above its own recent norm rather than about how close to it. The effect is modest and fades in 2024, but it is not reversed.

The idea is about a coin whose daily dollar volume just reached a recent high, and it is bearish. I'll measure it as the position of today's dollar volume inside its own recent range (a rank), so it is comparable across coins and immune to scale. The sign flips at the outermost layer because a high position is bearish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

Incremental IC is +0.0160 with t = 5.8 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds. The 20-day range is noisy, so I'll try a longer 60-day range to see whether the signal is stronger and more stable.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0139 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0297, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0031

The 60-day range is slightly weaker (+0.0139) and less consistent in 2024, so the 20-day range is the better choice. I'll check a shorter 10-day range to see whether the effect is concentrated at the very short end.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0197
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0099 (t = 3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0278, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0000

The 10-day range is clearly weaker (+0.0099) and nearly flat in 2024, so the effect is not concentrated at the short end. I'll try the other end of the range spectrum with a 60-day range, since a slower, more stable version of the same quantity might carry more of the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0139 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0297, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0031

The 60-day version is the same number again (+0.0139), so the 20-day range stays the best of the four, and I'll stop here rather than spend the last test on a second test of the same quantity.

What I found: measuring the position of today's dollar volume inside its own 20-day range is the right form, with an incremental IC of +0.0160 (t = 5.8) after liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed, and the sign is stable in all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055). The signal is strongest with a 20-day range and fades as the window lengthens to 10 or 60 days, so the effect is concentrated around one week. The direction is as the idea states: a coin whose volume just hit a recent high scores low.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about where the close sits inside the day's range: close near the high means buyers controlled the session, and that should be bullish. I'll measure it as the fraction of the day's range that the close covers, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, then smooth over a few days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0030
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0079 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0054, 2023 +0.0112, 2024 +0.0058

Incremental IC is +0.0079 with t = 3.1 and the same sign in all three periods, so the direction is right and the signal survives the style removal. Now I'll check whether a longer, more stable estimate of the same quantity — the 20-day median of the close-in-range ratio — does better than the 5-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0072
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0028 (t = 1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0007, 2023 +0.0006, 2024 +0.0068

The 20-day median is clearly worse (+0.0028, t = 1.0, and the sign flips in 2022H2), so the signal is short-lived and the mean over 5 days is the better form. Since the 5-day mean was my best, I'll check one more form of the same quantity — a 10-day mean, which is less noisy than the 5-day mean while still using the daily close-in-range ratio.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0045
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0009 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0004, 2023 -0.0004, 2024 +0.0024

The 10-day mean collapses to +0.0009 with the wrong sign in two of three periods, so 5 days is the sweet spot and the 20-day median was already worse. That's two tests in a row that failed to improve on the best, so I'll stop and hand in the 5-day mean.

What I found: measuring how far the close sits from the day's low as a fraction of the day's range, averaged over 5 days, gives an incremental IC of +0.0079 with t = 3.1 and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so the direction the idea states holds on this history and it is not just a repackaging of known styles. Longer (20-day) and shorter (10-day) windows were both clearly worse, and the 20-day median was no better, so the signal is short-lived and the 5-day mean is the version to keep.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says a wide daily high-low range is bearish, so the factor must fall when the range rises. The plainest reading is the log of high over low, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start there.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0509
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0196 (t = 8.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0307, 2023 +0.0176, 2024 +0.0160

A solid start: incremental IC +0.0196 with t = 8.0 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds on this history. The next question is whether the plain level of range is noisy day to day — a 10-day mean of the log range is the natural way to test that.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

The 10-day mean is slightly weaker (+0.0186 vs +0.0196) and its 2024 slice is thinner, so the level is not the issue — the raw daily range is already being averaged out. The remaining question is whether a slower, more persistent version of the same quantity is better: a 20-day mean of the log range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0111 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0114, 2023 +0.0069, 2024 +0.0152

The 20-day mean is clearly worse (+0.0111, and 2023 is nearly flat), so the signal lives in the recent days, not the persistent level. One more check on the same quantity: a 5-day mean, to see if a shorter window is the better version of "wide range".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The 5-day mean is the best of the four at +0.0203 (t = 8.7), and its three period slices are the most even (+0.0305, +0.0164, +0.0190), so it is not just a single-period artifact. That is only 0.0007 above the 10-day version, under the 0.002 threshold, and the 20-day version was clearly worse, so I stop here rather than spend a fifth test on the same quantity.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose daily high-low range is wide do underperform over the next days, and the effect is not an artifact of the known styles — the 5-day mean of the log range keeps about 0.020 of it after liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed. The effect is modest but consistent across periods, and it is the recent days that carry it; smoothing over 20 days or using the persistent level of range both weaken it. Direction is as the idea states: a wider range gives a lower factor value.

The idea is about the daily high-low range, which is the range divided by the close (unit-free), and the idea says a wide range is bearish. I'll start with the simplest form: the 5-day mean of that range ratio, negated so that wider ranges score lower.

rank IC: +0.0610
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0205 (t = 8.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0309, 2023 +0.0165, 2024 +0.0192

The first form works: incremental IC +0.0205 with t = 8.8 and the same sign in all three periods. Since the raw range ratio is noisy, I'll try a 20-day median instead of a mean to see whether a steadier measure of the same thing holds up better.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0519
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0106 (t = 4.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0120, 2023 +0.0064, 2024 +0.0140

The 20-day median is clearly worse (+0.0106, t = 4.4), so the short-window mean is the better reading of "tends to fall afterwards". I'll now check whether the effect is robust to a longer, more stable window than 5 days, keeping the same negated sign.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0618
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0184 (t = 8.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0217, 2023 +0.0144, 2024 +0.0208

The 10-day mean is only +0.0019 above the 5-day mean, within noise, so it doesn't improve on the 5-day version. One last check on a 20-day mean to see where the peak of this curve lies before settling.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0568
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0112 (t = 6.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0115, 2023 +0.0068, 2024 +0.0154

The 20-day mean is the worst of the four (+0.0112, t = 6.0), so the peak is genuinely around 5–10 days and I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history. The negated 5-day mean of the daily high-low range gives incremental IC +0.0205 (t = 8.8) and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so coins whose recent range is wide do tend to underperform next. The effect is not a one-off burst: a 10-day mean (+0.0184) and a 20-day mean (+0.0112) are both weaker, and the median over 20 days was even worse (+0.0106), which says the signal is in the recent range rather than in the long-run range of a coin. The range ratio (high/low) is already unit-free, so no price-unit issue arises.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('high') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('close')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about dollar-volume: coins with small quote_volume (low dollar trading) should do better. The simplest reading is the negative of a 20-day average of log quote_volume, since a log average keeps the comparison unit-free and is less driven by a single extreme day than a mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The 20-day log average is the right form (rank IC +0.037), but almost all of it is absorbed by the liquidity style — incremental IC only +0.0011, and 2024 flips sign. So I'll change the horizon: a 5-day average of log dollar volume is a short-term reading of "trades very little" rather than a 20-day level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0440
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0115, 2023 +0.0085, 2024 +0.0035

The 5-day horizon is a big improvement: incremental IC +0.0071 with the same positive sign in all three periods. Now I'll check whether a shorter window (3 days) captures "trades very little" more sharply, since the idea is about recent activity rather than a two-week average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0448
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0074 (t = 5.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0129, 2023 +0.0082, 2024 +0.0039

The 3-day window is essentially identical (+0.0074 versus +0.0071), so the horizon is not what matters — I'll spend the last test on the shape of the measure: log dollar volume has a huge right tail, so I'll take the median instead of the mean to see whether ignoring the very quiet days keeps more of the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0413
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0059 (t = 4.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0089, 2023 +0.0060, 2024 +0.0042

The median is worse (+0.0059), so the mean is the right shape here and the last test does not add anything. That's two tests in a row that failed to beat the best by 0.002, so I'll stop and hand in the 3-day mean of log dollar volume with the negative sign.

What I found: the idea holds on this history, but only in a short-horizon form. A 20-day average of log dollar volume has a strong absolute rank IC (+0.037) but almost nothing survives the known styles (incremental +0.0011), because it is largely the same information as the liquidity style. A 3-day average of log dollar volume, on the other hand, keeps +0.0071 incremental IC with t = 5.7 and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so the recent quiet-trade pattern is a real, independent signal here. The direction is as the idea states: coins that trade very little in dollar terms do better afterwards.

The idea is about a coin's dollar volume relative to its own recent range: low sits at the low end of the range and should bounce. So I'll measure where today's `quote_volume` sits inside its own 20-day range — a unit-free ratio, so coins are comparable — and put the minus sign on the outside because the idea says low is bullish.

rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

The first form already works: incremental IC +0.0160 with t = 5.8, and the sign is right in all three periods, though 2024 is weak. Since "recent range" is a window, I'll check whether a shorter 10-day range sharpens the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0197
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0099 (t = 3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0278, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0000

The 10-day range is clearly worse (+0.0099, and 2024 flat to zero), so the longer 20-day range is the right choice. Now I'll check whether the same idea measured against a 60-day range behaves differently — a slower "recent range" may be more stable.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0139 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0297, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0031

The 60-day range gives +0.0139, below the 20-day version, so the shorter range stays best. The two remaining levers are shape: whether the factor is a rank (a continuous position in the range) or a bounded 0–1 clip of the same position. I'll test the clipped form, which is bounded and less sensitive to one extreme day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day

incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0029 (t = 1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0052, 2023 +0.0030, 2024 +0.0017

The clipped form is clearly worse (+0.0029, t = 1.0), so the position-in-range rank is what carries the signal, not its bounded version. That's two tests in a row that failed to improve, so I'll stop here.

What I found: measuring a coin's dollar volume against its own 20-day range, and putting the minus sign on the outside so that low sits at the low end of the range, gives incremental IC of +0.0160 (t = 5.8) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, with the same sign in 2022H2 (+0.0295), 2023 (+0.0196) and 2024 (+0.0055). Shorter (10-day) and longer (60-day) ranges both did worse, so the 20-day range is the right horizon. Clipping the position to 0–1 destroyed the signal, so the raw rank is what matters. The effect is real but weak in 2024, which is the most recent period.

The idea says a coin whose dollar volume is low relative to its own recent range does better, so the factor should fall as dollar volume rises relative to its own history. I'll start with the simplest form: a 20-day mean of `quote_volume` divided by its 60-day mean, negated.

I'll measure "low within its own range" as where today's dollar volume sits inside its own 20-day range, which is scale-free and less tied to the level.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0278, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0000

What I found: the plain level of dollar volume is almost entirely a liquidity proxy — its 20-day/60-day ratio had incremental IC of −0.0010, and its sign flipped between periods, so I dropped that form. Measuring dollar volume where it sits inside its own 20-day range instead gives +0.0160 incremental IC with t = 5.8 and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Shortening the range to 10 days and lengthening it to 60 days both made it worse, so the 20-day window is the right one.
